FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)
INDIAN RED CROSS SOCIETY (IRCS) ACT

Que: What is Indian Red Cross Society (IRCS)?
Ans: IRCS is the largest statutory voluntary humanitarian organization that
works as Auxiliary to the Government and Armed Forces Medical services. It
was established under the Parliament Act XV of 1920.
Que: Who is the President of the IRCS?
Ans: Honorable President of India is the President of the IRCS.
Que: Who is the Chairman of the IRCS?
Ans: Hon'ble Union Health Minister is the Chairman of the Society.
Que: How many branches of IRCS work in India?

Ans: The IRCS has a network of over 1200 branches throughout the country.

Que: What is the function of IRCS across the country?

Ans: It contributes to saving lives and protecting livelihoods, provides relief
in times of disasters and other emergencies. It is a leading member of the
largest independent humanitarian organization in the world, the International
Red Cross & Red Crescent Movement. The movement has three main
components, the International Committee of Red Cross (ICRC), National
Societies and International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent
Societies.

Que: How is the Managing Body of the IRCS constituted and what are
its functions?
Ans: The National Managing Body which is the apex decision making body of
the IRCS, consists of 18 members. 6 members are nominated by the
President of India for such term as he/she may deem fit. The remaining 12
are elected by the State and Union Territory Branch committees for a term of
two years. The Managing Body is responsible for governance and supervision
of the functions of the society through a number of committees. The
Managing Body is for all practical purposes have complete control over the
financial and administrative matters of the Society including appointment,
termination and fixation of pay of its employees.
Que:Whether Government rules are applicable to the IRCS?
Ans: The government rules, per se, are not applicable ipso-facto to the IRCS or its
employees. However, in cases where the IRCS Act and Rules are silent on specific
matters, and no rules exist, such rules may be adopted by the Managing Body.

Que: What are the fundamental principles of the IRCS?
Ans: The IRCS follows 7 fundamental principles as given below:

(i)
Humanity

(ii)
Impartiality

(iii)
Neutrality

(iv)
Independence

(v)
Voluntary service

(vi)
Unity

(vii)
Universality
Que: Who has the power to make rules in the IRCS?
Ans: The Managing Body may, with the approval of the President make Rule
for the management, functions, control and procedure of the Society.
